notes: RTS ADAM CS is an "Advanced Digital Audio Matrix" — a digital intercom matrix mainframe, not a general audio DSP; closest available category taxonomy value used is "audio"/"DSP". Specs drawn from the manufacturer's own System Installation Guide (RTS/Bosch Security Systems, doc 9330-7517-000 Rev J, April 2009), fetched from products.rtsintercoms.com. The rear intercom-port panel ships in one of three mutually exclusive variants: RJ-11 (up to 64 ports, shown here as the default/primary configuration), 9-pin D-sub (DE-9P, up to 64 ports), or 50-pin Telco/Amphenol (9x 50-pin connectors, up to 64 ports via breakout). Only the RJ-11 variant is modeled here; a unit ordered with the DE-9P or Telco back panel would have different intercom-port connectors instead of the RJ-11 jacks listed. Each intercom port carries audio-in, audio-out, and data on the same connector (bidirectional in practice for keypanel/device connections), modeled here as one "input" and one "output" pair per port group for clarity is not applicable — ports are listed as bidirectional per the wiring diagrams (2-wire audio in, 2-wire audio out, 2-wire data all on one jack). Only a representative subset naming (e.g. J100-J107 for card 1) is included in full; total capacity is 64 RJ-11 intercom ports across 8 AIO cards (J100-J807), each following the same 2-conductor-pair pattern. No signal grades apply (no HDMI/SDI/USB/Ethernet/DisplayPort on this unit) — it is a legacy RS-232/RS-422 and analog/2-wire digital intercom matrix, so no ports have a "grade" field. Power: dual redundant AC inlets shown in back-panel diagrams as standard IEC-style receptacles with integral fuse/switch (AC1 to PS1, AC2 to PS2); exact IEC sub-type (C13/C14) is inferred from diagram graphics, not stated as a numeric standard in the document — confidence on this specific point is medium, though the overall port inventory is high-confidence manufacturer data. J903 GPI port is DB-25S (mapped to rs232 connector family absence — modeled as db-25 not in allowed list, so approximated as the closest serial connector "rs232" is inaccurate; see below). The allowed connector enum has no DB-25 option, so J900/J901/J902 (true DE-9/DB-9 D-sub serial ports) are mapped to "rs232", and J903 (DB-25S) is also approximated as "rs232" since DB-25 is not in the enum — this is a forced approximation, not an exact match.

ports.name: Intercom Port J100 (Card 1, Port 1)
ports.note: RJ-11 6-pin jack carrying 2-wire audio-to-matrix, 2-wire audio-from-matrix, and 2-wire data. Approximated as rj45 (closest connector in allowed list); actual connector is RJ-11/RJ-12 6P6C, not RJ45 8P8C.

ports.name: Intercom Ports J101–J807 (64 total, Cards 1–8)
ports.note: Remaining 63 RJ-11 intercom ports (8 AIO cards x 8 ports each) for keypanels, camera delegate panels, program inputs, TIF-951 telephone interfaces, etc. Same wiring as J100. Alternate back-panel variants (ordered separately) replace all RJ-11 jacks with DE-9P D-sub or 50-pin Telco connectors instead.

ports.name: J900 (RS232 to Configuration PC)
ports.note: DE-9S (9-pin D-sub) serial port for AZedit configuration software connection (null-modem cable to PC COM port).

ports.name: J901 (RS422/232 to Trunk Master)
ports.note: DE-9S connector for RS422/232 connection to an RTS Intelligent Trunking system master.

ports.name: J902 (RS422/232 to Accessories)
ports.note: DE-9S connector for RS422/232 connection of Program Assign Panels (PAP), LCP-102 Level Control Panels, and UIO-256/GPIO-16 Universal I/O frames.

ports.name: J903 (General Purpose I/O)
ports.note: DB-25S (25-pin D-sub) connector providing 8 digital (GPI) inputs and 8 open-collector digital outputs. Approximated as rs232 connector id; actual physical connector is a DB-25, not in the allowed connector list.

ports.name: AC1 (Power Supply 1 Input)
ports.note: Fused AC inlet with on/off switch, feeds internal Power Supply 1 (PS1). Exact IEC sub-type (C13/C14) inferred from back-panel diagram; not explicitly specified in the document.

ports.name: AC2 (Power Supply 2 Input)
ports.note: Fused AC inlet with on/off switch, feeds internal Power Supply 2 (PS2) for redundant operation; can be wired to a separate AC phase for additional resiliency.
